sections.title: The letter i
paragraphs: You name this letter (i) /i/. Its main sound is a vowel, heard in the word (ilha) /ˈi.ʎɐ/, which means island. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter has two sounds in European Portuguese.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, push your tongue high and forward. Spread your lips wide like a smile, and turn your voice on. For the second sound, make your mouth narrower. Glide your tongue very quickly toward the roof of the mouth. Touch your throat with two fingers. You will feel your vocal cords shake for both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter makes the vowel sound when it forms the centre of a syllable. You hear this sound in (amigo) /ɐ.ˈmi.ɡu/. It makes a short glide sound called a semivowel when it sits next to another vowel in the same beat. A semivowel is a short sound that works like a vowel but acts like a consonant. You hear this glide in (pai) /ˈpaj/ and in (viagem) /ˈvja.ʒɐ̃j̃/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say the short vowel in English sit. Keep your tongue higher and spread your lips wider, like the sound in see. When this letter stands next to another vowel, do not stretch it into an extra syllable. Glide smoothly from one sound to the next without a pause.
